summary: The change does what was asked. On every run, the throughput review now compares the latest stage medians with the previous review's before it checks for an open design request (`compare_with_previous_review`, called at hestia.rs:1644). It names the stages that grew, largest first, in the review note, in the line `athena drain` prints and in a line to the person running the review. When the median rose by more than 25% (`SLOWDOWN_RATIO = 1.25`, enforced in `is_slowdown`), code queues a high-priority request through `StewardRequest`/`self.queue` without asking the model. That request is titled `Throughput slowdown: <stage> grew from <prev> to <now> min per landed job`, and an open one holds back a second. The previous stage medians are rebuilt from the job records (`landed_jobs_among_first`, `StageMinutes::median_of`), so the record schema does not change; records.rs gets doc comments only. I ran `cargo test -p athena-core hestia` (49 passed, including all the new tests and the existing throughput tests, unchanged) and the new status.rs test. fmt, clippy and the full test suite pass per Athena's CI records. All five changed files are on the deliverables list. The docs (module comment, hestia.md "Slowdown" paragraph, CHANGELOG) match the code. I found no blocker or major problem.
